newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes firmer as wheat recovers late.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes firmer as wheat recovers late.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed firmer on a late and abrupt recovery from session lows in wheat that was tied to a report crop observers pegged recent freeze losses in the hard red winter wheat crop at a level above expectations, traders said.
Wheat and corn sagged in early dealings on signals the wheat market was technically overbought after the recent rally to contract highs in the deferred months.

Corn futures were consolidating at a level slightly above the 50-day moving average (MA) which in the July, closed at $2.97 per bushel. The session low for July was $2.98-1/2. The 40-day MA was at $3.01-1/2 at 1045 and first resistance in the July was at $3.02-1/2 and first support was at $2.98-1/2.

Slow farmer selling gave the market some underpinning with the December firm on forecasts for cool, damp weather in much of the U.S. corn growing region. That scenario could slow the corn seeding pace, traders said.
USDA said as of Sunday, seven percent of U.S. corn had been planted, slightly behind nine percent a year ago but the same as the seven-percent average.
Corn ended 1-1/2 cents a bushel higher to 3/4 lower, with May up 1-1/2 at $3.01-1/4.
July closed 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher at $3.02.
